articles.summary: Key Takeaways A healthy scalp microbiome helps maintain scalp balance. Beneficial microorganisms support the scalp's natural environment and help keep the ecosystem functioning properly. Scalp health influences hair health. An imbalanced microbiome may contribute to scalp concerns such as irritation, dryness, excess oil, or visible flaking. The scalp's pH plays an important role. A slightly acidic environment helps support the microorganisms that naturally live on the scalp. Overwashing and underwashing can disrupt balance. Finding the right cleansing frequency helps support both the scalp barrier and microbiome. Personalized products can support unique scalp needs. Tailoring your routine to concerns like oiliness, dryness, sensitivity, or visible flakes can help maintain a healthier scalp environment.

articles.summary: Key Takeaways Hair slugging helps reduce moisture loss overnight. The technique creates a protective barrier that helps the hair retain hydration while you sleep. Dry hair is often a moisture retention issue. Hair slugging helps support the cuticle's ability to hold onto moisture, especially for dry, damaged, curly, or coily hair. Not all hair types need the same level of slugging. Fine and straight hair may benefit from lightweight leave-ins, while curly and coily hair often need richer moisture support. The right products matter. Leave-in conditioners, hair masks, serums, and curl creams each support moisture retention differently depending on your hair's structure. Hair slugging works best when paired with protective fabrics. Silk or satin wraps help reduce friction, preserve moisture, and minimize breakage while you sleep.
